cells.tense: What you can imagine is moving you now, before you can explain it.
cells.ask: Take one thing that has been moving you and bring it all the way through to done. Then leave a whole day empty before you pick up the next one.
cells.core:
You can feel your way into something half-formed and stay with it until it tells you what it is. That is not a mood you fall into — it is a way of working, and it is running right now. What you picture and what you do are the same motion, which is why the things around you actually get finished instead of piling up as ideas.
You get to trust that. The pull that keeps you moving will still be there after you stop for a minute and let one piece land. Finish this cleanly, then take a day that is about nothing. The next thing opens better from rest than from generosity.

cells.verb: opening to what is not yet known and letting it move you
cells.place: the doorway where what has been made is finished and let go

cells.tense: You are living in a version of this that has not arrived yet, and bracing for it.
cells.ask: Write the next small step for one thing you keep imagining, and stop at that line. Put the pen down before you plan the rest of it.
cells.core:
There is a version ahead where it is already finished and good, and some part of you is living there. You feel out what is coming faster than it comes, so the listening turns into steering — the shape has to be right before it has even been built, the timing has to land on schedule. The reach itself is fine. The grip is what costs you.
After something is worked through, this settles into something plainer: you imagine, you build, you finish, you let the next one wait its turn. Hold this lightly and let it look after itself. You will get more out of the next stretch that way than out of another late night spent getting it exactly right.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a doorway that has already closed behind you.
cells.ask: Say one plain sentence out loud about what you meant to finish. Let one person tell you what they notice, and keep it.
cells.core:
There is something you feel toward and do not go after. The sensing is still in you — it just stopped turning into anything you can point to. When nothing gets decided, whichever pull is loudest wins, and it is rarely the one you would have chosen. Meanwhile the finished things, and the feeling of having landed somewhere, stay out of reach.
You do not have to have an answer before you say you do not have one. This works when you notice something, say it badly, and someone hands back a piece of it. Telling one person what you vaguely sense will do more than another hour of circling alone. Something solid tends to show up once you are not the only one holding it.

cells.tense: The pen is down in a room you are already writing, and you call it undecided.
cells.ask: Name one thing you have already chosen to shape, and say out loud that it is yours. Once is enough.
cells.core:
You are already making something — picking, feeling out, leaning one way more than another — and the people near you can tell which way it leans. But you describe it as no big deal, or as just what is happening around you. The making is running. No credit has gone back to the one doing it.
Say what you are making and the work gets easier instead of heavier. Own one choice out loud and the rest of the noise quiets down. Not a promise, not a plan. One thing you settle on, said once, in your own voice.

attempts.check: Nothing in the record says what any of their hopes, disappointments, or circumstances actually are, so no cell may supply a scene and call it their life. A reader could reasonably say 'bad timing isn't my problem — the volume is' if their excess doesn't look like haste, which is why the ask is scaled to one visible act. The ask survives being wrong about the status entirely: a single thing taken through to done is useful whether they are too fast, too late, or already finished and not saying so. The sentence that would serve the writing more than the person would be anything that admires the shifting, unfinished feel of this card instead of naming what it does to them.
